## CLUE: A Chinese Language Understanding Evaluation Benchmark

The paper "CLUE: A Chinese Language Understanding Evaluation Benchmark" was published by Xu et al. at COLING 2020 (the 28th International Conference on Computational Linguistics), appearing on pages 4762–4772 in Barcelona, Spain.

### Overview

CLUE is an open-ended, community-driven project that brings together 9 tasks spanning several well-established single-sentence/sentence-pair classification tasks, as well as machine reading comprehension, all on original Chinese text.

### Motivation and Contribution

Most existing benchmarks like GLUE and SuperGLUE are limited to English, which has made it difficult to replicate many successes in English NLU for other languages. To help remedy this issue, the authors introduced the first large-scale Chinese Language Understanding Evaluation (CLUE) benchmark.

### Methodology and Resources

To establish results on these tasks, the authors report scores using an exhaustive set of current state-of-the-art pre-trained Chinese models (9 in total). They also introduce a number of supplementary datasets and additional tools to help facilitate further progress on Chinese NLU.

The benchmark is publicly available at https://www.cluebenchmarks.com.

## Publication Details

Watson and Crick published their findings in a one-page paper, with the understated title "A Structure for Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid," in the British scientific weekly Nature on April 25, 1953. It was published on pages 737–738 of its 171st volume (dated 25 April 1953).

## The Discovery

The discovery in 1953 of the double helix, the twisted-ladder structure of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), by James Watson and Francis Crick marked a milestone in the history of science and gave rise to modern molecular biology.

## Key Structural Features

The paper described several important features of DNA:

- If A always paired with T, and likewise C with G, then not only were Chargaff's rules accounted for, but the pairs could be neatly fitted between the two helical sugar-phosphate backbones of DNA, the outside rails of the ladder

- The bases connected to the two backbones at right angles while the backbones retained their regular shape as they wound around a common axis, all of which were structural features demanded by the X-ray evidence

## Significance

In the words of Watson and Crick: "It has not escaped our notice that the specific pairing that we have postulated immediately suggests a possible copying mechanism for the genetic material."

## Overview
The paper was authored by Mandar Joshi, Eunsol Choi, Daniel Weld, and Luke Zettlemoyer, and published in the Proceedings of the 55th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics in 2017.

## Dataset Description
TriviaQA is a challenging reading comprehension dataset containing over 650K question-answer-evidence triples, with 95K question-answer pairs authored by trivia enthusiasts and independently gathered evidence documents—six per question on average—that provide high quality distant supervision for answering the questions.

## Key Characteristics
Compared to other recently introduced large-scale datasets, TriviaQA (1) has relatively complex, compositional questions, (2) has considerable syntactic and lexical variability between questions and corresponding answer-evidence sentences, and (3) requires more cross sentence reasoning to find answers.

## Performance
The paper presents two baseline algorithms: a feature-based classifier and a state-of-the-art neural network that performs well on SQuAD reading comprehension. Neither approach comes close to human performance (23% and 40% vs. 80%), suggesting that TriviaQA is a challenging testbed.

## Main Contribution

The paper addresses the challenge that deeper neural networks are more difficult to train, and presents a residual learning framework to ease the training of networks that are substantially deeper than those used previously.(no content)The key innovation involves explicitly reformulating layers as learning residual functions with reference to the layer inputs, instead of learning unreferenced functions.

## Key Results and Impact

On the ImageNet dataset, the researchers evaluated residual networks with a depth of up to 152 layers—8× deeper than VGG nets but still having lower complexity.(no content)The results won 1st place on the ILSVRC 2015 classification task, and deep residual networks were foundations of their submissions to ILSVRC & COCO 2015 competitions, where they also won 1st places on ImageNet detection, ImageNet localization, COCO detection, and COCO segmentation.

## Architecture Overview

ResNets are a type of convolutional neural network where the input from the previous layer is added to the output of the current layer, with skip connections that make it easier for the network to learn and result in better performance.

## Overview

"BoolQ: Exploring the Surprising Difficulty of Natural Yes/No Questions" was published by Clark et al. at the 2019 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics (NAACL).

## Dataset Description

The paper studies yes/no questions that are naturally occurring—generated in unprompted and unconstrained settings—and builds a reading comprehension dataset called BoolQ of such questions. BoolQ is a question answering dataset for yes/no questions containing 15,942 examples.

## Key Findings

The dataset shows that naturally occurring yes/no questions are unexpectedly challenging, as they often query for complex, non-factoid information and require difficult entailment-like inference to solve.

## Results

The researchers find that transferring from entailment data is more effective than transferring from paraphrase or extractive QA data, and that it surprisingly continues to be very beneficial even when starting from massive pre-trained language models such as BERT. Their best method achieves 80.4% accuracy compared to 90% accuracy of human annotators (and 62% majority-baseline).

LILA is a unified mathematical reasoning benchmark consisting of 23 diverse tasks along four dimensions: (i) mathematical abilities e.g., arithmetic, calculus (ii) language format e.g., question-answering, fill-in-the-blanks (iii) language diversity e.g., no language, simple language (iv) external knowledge e.g., commonsense, physics.

## Overview

The paper "Adversarial Watermarking Transformer: Towards Tracing Text Provenance with Data Hiding" was authored by Sahar Abdelnabi and Mario Fritz and published in the 42nd IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy in 2021.

## Key Contributions

The paper introduces the Adversarial Watermarking Transformer (AWT) with a jointly trained encoder-decoder and adversarial training that, given an input text and a binary message, generates an output text that is unobtrusively encoded with the given message. The researchers study different training and inference strategies to achieve minimal changes to the semantics and correctness of the input text. AWT is the first end-to-end model to hide data in text by automatically learning word substitutions along with their locations without ground truth.

## Research Focus

The paper addresses concerns about the potential misuse of powerful language models for malicious purposes and studies natural language watermarking as a defense to help better mark and trace the provenance of text.

The paper is available on multiple platforms including:

## Overview

Meteor is a cryptographically secure steganography system by Gabriel Kaptchuk, Tushar M. Jois, Matthew Green, and Aviel Rubin that addresses practical steganographic systems capable of embedding messages into realistic communication distributions like text.

## Key Challenges Addressed

The paper identifies two primary impediments to deploying universal steganography: (1) prior work leaves the difficult problem of finding samplers for non-trivial distributions unaddressed, and (2) prior constructions have impractical minimum entropy requirements.

## Technical Approach

The authors investigate using generative models as steganographic samplers, as they represent the best known technique for approximating human communication. They design a new steganographic protocol called Meteor to overcome the entropy requirement.

## Key Results

The resulting protocols are provably indistinguishable from honest model output and represent an important step towards practical steganographic communication for mundane communication channels. The authors implement Meteor and evaluate it on multiple computation environments with multiple generative models.

## Publication

The paper was published at ACM CCS 2021, with the paper available on the IACR ePrint archive as well as through ACM's digital library.

The paper "Efficiently Identifying Watermarked Segments in Mixed-Source Texts" by Xuandong Zhao, Chenwen Liao, Yu-Xiang Wang, and Lei Li was published in the Proceedings of the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL 2025) in July 2025 in Vienna, Austria.

## Overview

Text watermarks in large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to detect synthetic text, mitigating misuse cases like fake news and academic dishonesty. While existing watermarking detection techniques primarily focus on classifying entire documents as watermarked or not, they often neglect the common scenario of identifying individual watermark segments within longer, mixed-source documents.

## Methodology

The paper proposes two novel methods for partial watermark detection. First, they develop a geometry cover detection framework aimed at determining whether there is a watermark segment in long text. Second, they introduce an adaptive online learning algorithm to pinpoint the precise location of watermark segments within the text.

## Results

Evaluated on three popular watermarking techniques (KGW-Watermark, Unigram-Watermark, and Gumbel-Watermark), their approach achieves high accuracy, significantly outperforming baseline methods.

## Paper Overview

Natural language watermarking (NLW) is a technique designed to help trace the provenance of texts for protecting against possible attacks, where the watermark signals are embedded into cover texts using synonym substitutions.

## The Qiang et al. 2023 Contribution

The study proposes a novel NLW method by incorporating a paraphraser-based lexical substitution method. Under the promise of paraphrase preservation, the proposed NLW method utilizes the knowledge of paraphrase modeling to generate the substitute candidates to replace the words in original sentences capable of carrying the watermark signal in local contexts.

## Key Improvements

The NLW method not only has better meaning-preserved quality, but improves the payload more than 2 times compared with the BERT-based NLW method. Additionally, the experimental results show that the proposed LS method improves the Precision@1 score from 51.7% to 58.3% and from 50.5% to 62.6% on LS07 and CoInCo benchmarks, respectively.

## Why This Approach?

BERT entirely or partially masks the target word of original text to generate corresponding substitute candidates. Nevertheless, BERT trained on raw data cannot pertinently learn the operation of lexical substitution. There are many words that only fit for the context without considering the meaning of the target word that are generated as the substitutes leading to a low watermark embedding capacity.

The paper was published in Artificial Intelligence in 2023, with code available on GitHub.

### Overview

The paper addresses a critical security risk in LLM agents: indirect prompt injection, which compromises the core of these agents by manipulating contextual information rather than direct user prompts.

### Methodology

The paper proposes a generic black-box optimization framework, AGENTVIGIL, designed to automatically discover and exploit indirect prompt injection vulnerabilities across diverse LLM agents. The approach starts by constructing a high-quality initial seed corpus, then employs a seed selection algorithm based on Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) to iteratively refine inputs, thereby maximizing the likelihood of uncovering agent weaknesses.
